record.paper_title: Some Open Questions about Symplectic 4-Manifolds, Singular Plane Curves, and Braid Group Factorizations
record.original_question: For fixed integers d, ν, κ, and N, classify all pairs (D, θ) up to admissible regular homotopy, where D is a symplectic degree-d curve in CP^2 with ν_+ positive nodes, ν_- negative nodes, and κ complex cusps satisfying ν_+ - ν_- = ν, and θ: π_1(CP^2 - D) → S_N is a compatible monodromy homomorphism. Here an admissible regular homotopy is a regular homotopy through such branch curves in which any creation of a node pair is allowed only when the two local geometric generators are sent by θ to transpositions on disjoint pairs of sheets.

evidence.quote: Question 3.11. Given integers (d, ν, κ, N), can one classify all pairs (D, θ) where D is a symplectic curve of degree d in CP^2 with ν+ positive nodes, ν− negative nodes and κ complex cusps, ν+ − ν− = ν, and θ : π1(CP^2 − D) → S_N is a compatible monodromy morphism, up to admissible regular homotopies?

The requirement for admissibility of a node creation operation is that the images by θ of these two geometric generators should be transpositions acting on disjoint pairs of elements (i.e., the branching phenomena above the two intersecting branches of D should occur in different sheets of the covering).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix positive integers $d$, $N$, a nonnegative integer $\kappa$, and an integer $\nu$. Consider pairs $(D,\theta)$ where:

(a) $D \subset \mathbb{CP}^2$ is a symplectic curve of degree $d$ whose only singularities are transverse double points (nodes) and complex cusps; the nodes are split into $\nu_+$ positive nodes and $\nu_-$ negative nodes with $\nu_+ - \nu_- = \nu$, and the number of cusps is $\kappa$;

(b) $\theta\colon \pi_1(\mathbb{CP}^2 \setminus D) \to S_N$ is a compatible monodromy homomorphism, i.e.\ it sends each positively oriented meridian (geometric generator) around a smooth branch of $D$ to a transposition in $S_N$, and the relations imposed by the local models at the nodes and cusps are satisfied.

Define an admissible regular homotopy between two such pairs $(D_0,\theta_0)$ and $(D_1,\theta_1)$ to be a one-parameter family $(D_t,\theta_t)$ of pairs of the above form, where $D_t$ is a regular homotopy of symplectic immersed curves (so that generically $D_t$ has only nodes and cusps, with finitely many degenerations along the way), $\theta_t$ varies continuously with $t$, and the only permitted node creation/annihilation moves are those for which the two local geometric generators meeting at the created/annihilated node pair are mapped by $\theta_t$ to transpositions acting on disjoint pairs of sheets of the $N$-fold cover.

Problem. Classify all such pairs $(D,\theta)$ up to admissible regular homotopy, in terms of the fixed data $(d,\nu,\kappa,N)$.
artifact.category_tag: Symplectic branch curves and braid monodromy
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open classification problem. A related result of Auroux–Kulikov–Shevchishin establishes that irreducible symplectic cuspidal curves in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ of fixed degree with prescribed numbers of (positive) nodes and cusps are regular homotopic, which addresses the case without the monodromy datum $\theta$ and without negative nodes. No source found that classifies the pairs $(D,\theta)$ in the general admissible setting; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Regular homotopy of Hurwitz curves (Auroux–Kulikov–Shevchishin)
status_evidence.snippet: Any two irreducible cuspidal Hurwitz curves with the same homology class and the same set of singularities in a Hirzebruch surface are regular homotopic; symplectically regular homotopic if symplectic.
status_evidence.claim: A related (weaker) classification up to regular homotopy is known, but the refined classification of pairs (D,θ) up to admissible regular homotopy is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Questions about Symplectic 4-Manifolds, Singular Plane Curves, and Braid Group Factorizations
status_evidence.snippet: The classification of pairs (D,θ) up to admissible regular homotopy is stated as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is presented as an open question.
